Scope rules:
A playlist is visible and editable under the capability on its owning scope; a company playlist is visible to anyone with `programming.view` anywhere in the company and editable with company-wide `programming.edit`.
A group, its program and its branch span need the capability on every branch of the span; a whole-company group needs company scope. A group that a person can see only partly does not exist for them (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
A screen's own program and settings need the capability on the screen's branch. Joining a group needs `programming.assign` on the screen's branch and on every branch of the group's span.
A screen's views never reveal what the caller cannot see. A screen in a group the caller sees only partly reports a group source with no group, and its timeline still shows what the screen plays; leaving that group needs only `programming.assign` on the screen's branch. A playlist outside the caller's scope, such as one of a moved screen's previous branch, keeps its ID without a summary.
A rule or default may use a playlist only when every branch the program can reach is inside the playlist's scope: company playlists always, a branch playlist only for that branch's screens or for a group whose span is exactly that branch.
The capabilities follow the existing assurance rule for standard roles; profiles set it per capability.

title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Per company: 1,000 playlists, 100 groups, 2,000 programs. Per playlist 500 items; per output 200 rules. A timeline request covers at most 31 days and 2,000 segments. Exceeding a count limit returns `PROGRAMMING_LIMIT_REACHED`, whose message names the limits; a transaction-scoped lock per company serializes each count with its insert, so concurrent creations cannot pass a limit; list and rule-set sizes beyond their maximum fail request validation.

title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Audit
text:
Audit
Every creation, edit, deletion and assignment writes a programming audit event with the actor's membership, the subject (playlist, group, program or screen), the branches it concerns and a bounded summary (names, counts and versions, never media content), in the same transaction as the change. Viewing follows the organization audit rules: administrators see all, managers see events of their branches.

title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Contracts
text:
Contracts
Versioned JSON operations under `/companies/{companyId}/programming/...` for playlists (list with scope and name filters and cursors, create, get, rename, replace items, change transition, delete), groups (list, create, get, rename, change span, delete), group and device programs (get, replace one output's rules and default), device settings (get, assign), the rule check and the two timelines; plus the time-zone field on device detail and update. title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Panel
text:
Panel
A **Programação** area per company (en-US "Programming"), shown with `programming.view`:
**Playlists**: list with scope and search; the editor adds ready media from the library through a picker filtered by the playlist's scope, reorders items with buttons and keyboard, edits image durations, shows total duration and saves the whole list.

**Schedules editor**: one row per rule (playlist, weekdays, all-day or times, dates), the default playlist, conflict errors next to both rules, and a seven-day local timeline with resolution notes.
Copy is in `pt-BR` and `en-US`, times use the person's locale with the screen's zone named, and every control is reachable by keyboard.

title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
**Program model.** Reusable playlists owned like media (company or one branch); one program per group and per screen; a screen without a group, or with individual programming selected, uses its own program; one full-screen output now, with layout areas as further outputs in PJ-20.
**Group span.** A group covers the whole company or a fixed set of branches; only screens of those branches join; authority over a group requires authority over every branch of its span.
**Rule representation.** ISO weekdays, local start and end at minute precision, an explicit all-day flag, a first date and an optional inclusive final date; no zone stored on rules; the zone comes from the screen, otherwise its branch.
**Conflict validation.** Reject overlapping windows on the same output by comparing them in local wall-clock time, independent of zones, over the complete rule set saved atomically; touching windows are allowed.
**DST handoff refinement.** Gaps resolve to the first valid instant and repeated hours to the earlier occurrence for starts and the later for ends, as selected; additionally, an end never extends past the next window's start on the same output. This refines P14 so that two close windows can never overlap in a repeated hour, which wall-clock validation cannot see, instead of rejecting otherwise valid schedules in zones with DST.
**Evaluator and library (ADR-0029).** A pure TypeScript evaluator in the API on the Temporal API through the `temporal-polyfill` package until Node.js ships Temporal; canonical JSON fixtures owned by the API and run by the player in PJ-12; preview computed only by the API.
**Items and transitions.** Images 1 to 3,600 s (10 s default), videos at full duration, playlists loop, boundaries interrupt; transitions `CUT` or `FADE` of 250 to 2,000 ms, with fades accepted at publication only on qualified profiles.
**Permissions.** `programming.view`, `programming.edit` and `programming.assign` as in the table, all delegable; operators author drafts but do not assign; assigning needs strong authentication like managing screens.
**Assignment confirmation.** Assignments are separate from program edits, use the screen's settings version and require an explicit confirmation while the destination is unpublished, which is every destination until PJ-11.
**Lifecycle.** Playlists and groups are deleted only when unused, with a confirmation; media used by playlists cannot be deleted; archived media stays in playlists but cannot be added.
**Limits.** 1,000 playlists, 100 groups and 2,000 programs per company; 500 items per playlist; 200 rules per output; timelines of 31 days and 2,000 segments.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-10 in local and CI environments. It does not publish anything to screens (PJ-11), qualify fades or schedule timing on hardware (PH-08, PJ-12) or design layout areas (PJ-20).

title: Teluni Programming Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**Store each rule's time zone, or a group zone.** It would let a group run on one zone's clock, but the selected policy interprets local hours per screen, and a stored zone would diverge from branch changes.
**Store expanded occurrences.** Simple queries, but unbounded for open-ended rules and wrong after a zone database update; evaluating from rules keeps one source of truth.
**iCalendar RRULE strings.** A standard, but far more expressive than the selected rules (monthly, by-set positions, exceptions), harder to validate for conflicts and to explain in the panel; the weekday model covers FR-06 and can export to RRULE later.
**Validate conflicts on resolved instants per zone.** Exact, but depends on every zone a group can reach and on future zone-database changes, and still needs the repeated-hour rule; wall-clock validation plus the handoff clip is zone-independent and deterministic.
**Luxon or date-fns-tz.** Mature, but each has its own model of gaps and repeated hours; Temporal's model matches `java.time`, which the Android player is expected to use, so both implementations reason in the same terms.
**Hand-written arithmetic over `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.** No dependency, but transition search and disambiguation are where subtle bugs live; a spec-conformant implementation tested against the shared fixtures is safer.
**Implicit priority between overlapping rules.** Rejected by the policies.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-04 (server side) and the basic monitoring of FR-09, 2026-10-20.** The owner approved all ten [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed under [PH-25](human-actions.md#ph-25), including ADR-0030, after the API and panel had been built on the recommended options so the review could see working behavior. Approval authorizes PJ-11 in local and CI environments with a simulated player.
In scope: publishing a program into an immutable generation, the manifest format, the desired publication of each screen, the device synchronization exchange, delivery of manifests and media to screens, the signed authorization statement, acknowledgements and state reports, the screen's synchronization state in the panel, published-reference protection, publication history, restore and retention, permissions, limits, audit, data, contracts and verification (FR-07, FR-09).
Out of scope, with their owners: the player's storage, staging, activation and power-loss recovery, which this design states only as obligations of the protocol (D-07, PJ-12); trusted-time estimation on the device (D-07, AT-16), which receives a signed server time here; layout areas and catalog snapshots (D-11, PJ-20/PJ-21), which extend the manifest; automatic price publication (PJ-21); optional publication approvals (IA-12, PJ-24); commercial expiry capping and transfer accounting (PJ-27); alerts, diagnostic records and support tools (D-09); push notifications, which this design does not need; qualification on hardware (PH-08).

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Edits are drafts until deliberately published. A publication is an immutable, complete snapshot; activation needs its whole supported resource set, and failure preserves the last valid generation. Distinguish saved, published, downloaded and active states; server intent is never activation evidence ([assignment and publication](release-policies.md#assignment-and-publication), [publication lifecycle](playback-and-sync.md#publication-lifecycle)).
Confirming an assignment requests the destination's latest publication without another publish action. An intentionally unpublished destination is allowed after a clear indication and then shows neutral output; a failed or unseen synchronization preserves valid state.
Order desired state by authoritative server state, never by device clocks; old acknowledgements cannot roll a screen back; superseded delivery work may coalesce to the latest authorized compatible snapshot ([consistency](playback-and-sync.md#consistency-and-concurrency)).
Detect a desired publication within 30 seconds (AT-11); report state every 30 seconds, stale after 90 seconds and offline after 120 seconds, always with the last observed time (AT-24); show an observed acknowledgement within 10 seconds of receiving it (AT-14).
Offline authorization ends no later than seven days after the last renewal (AT-15); trusted-time uncertainty of at most 60 seconds (AT-16); the player keeps the active and previous valid generations and a valid staging attempt (AT-19) within the reserve of AT-05.
Inactive publication history stays recoverable for at least 90 days (AT-18); detailed operational reports are kept 30 days by default (AT-20); the current and previous protocol generations are supported for at least 90 days after a transition (AT-26).
Publishing or restoring a published version is allowed to administrators company-wide and branch managers in their branches; operators need an additional grant ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Anyone granted publication needs strong authentication, and ordinary publication uses the normal compliant session without a new prompt.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Concepts
text:
Concepts
A **destination** is a program of the programming module: a group's program or a screen's own program.
A **publication** is one immutable generation of a destination. Generations count 1, 2, 3 per program. A publication holds the manifest's exact bytes, their SHA-256, a digest of its content, the media it needs, its publisher and time.
A screen's **desired publication** is the latest publication of its current programming source; a screen whose source has none desires nothing and shows neutral output.
A screen's **reported state** is what it says it received, staged and activated. Reports are facts about the screen, never instructions to the server.

heading: Publishing

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: The manifest
text:
The manifest
The manifest is UTF-8 JSON produced by the server in a fixed key order without insignificant whitespace, stored and served byte for byte, and identified by the SHA-256 of those bytes. Protocol 1:
{
  "format": "teluni.publication",
  "protocol": 1,
  "publicationId": "…",
  "companyId": "…",
  "programId": "…",
  "generation": 3,
  "publishedAt": "2026-10-19T12:00:00.000Z",
  "outputs": [
    {
      "key": "screen",
      "defaultPlaylistId": null,
      "rules": [
        {
          "id": "…",
          "playlistId": "…",
          "weekdays": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
          "allDay": false,
          "startTime": "08:00",
          "endTime": "18:00",
          "startsOn": "2026-10-20",
          "endsOn": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "playlists": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "transition": { "kind": "CUT" },
      "items": [{ "mediaId": "…", "durationMs": 10000 }]
    }
  ],
  "media": [
    {
      "id": "…",
      "kind": "IMAGE",
      "contentType": "image/jpeg",
      "size": 482113,
      "sha256": "…",
      "width": 1920,
      "height": 1080,
      "durationMs": null,
      "hasAudio": false
    }
  ]
}

Rules use the exact representation of the [shared schedule fixtures](programming-design.md#shared-fixtures), so the player evaluates a manifest with the same code it tests against the fixtures. The time zone is not part of the manifest: one group publication serves screens in different zones, and each screen receives its zone with its desired state. Names of playlists, media and people are omitted; the player does not show them, and identifiers are enough for diagnostics. A video item's `durationMs` is null: it plays its whole rendition.
The content digest is the SHA-256 of the same serialization of `outputs`, `playlists` and `media` only, so it does not change with the generation, time or identifiers of a publication.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Desired state
text:
Desired state
The desired publication of a screen is computed when the screen synchronizes, from current rows: the screen's programming settings choose the source (its group's program unless individual programming is selected, otherwise its own), and the source's latest publication is desired. Nothing is fanned out when someone publishes or assigns: a new publication, an assignment, a move that leaves a group or a group change takes effect at the screen's next synchronization, at most 30 seconds later while it is connected. Because desired state always comes from authoritative rows, an old acknowledgement or a reordered report cannot roll a screen back.
The programming module's assignment confirmation becomes exact: `confirmUnpublished` is required only when the destination has no publication, and the panel then explains that the screen will show neutral output until the destination is published. A destination with a publication needs no confirmation; the screen moves to that destination's latest publication. This completes the programming design's increment 3 for publications.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Synchronization exchange
text:
Synchronization exchange
Screens use their device credential (ADR-0027) on every request and poll; the server never pushes.
Operation
Purpose
`POST /device/sync`
Every 30 seconds: the screen sends its state report and receives its status, time zone, desired publication and a fresh authorization statement
`GET /device/publications/{publicationId}/manifest`
The manifest bytes of the screen's current desired publication
`GET /device/media/{mediaId}`
The display rendition of a media item of the current desired publication, with single-range requests for resuming
`GET /device/keys`
The public keys that verify authorization statements
The sync response carries `serverTime`; `status` (`active`, `suspended` or `unlinked`, as in `GET /device/self`); the effective `timeZone` (the screen's own, otherwise its branch's) with `zoneOffsets`, its UTC offsets from three days before `serverTime` to 35 days after it, and the configured `rotation`, both added for the player ([player design](player-design.md#server-additions)); `desired` with the publication ID, generation, manifest SHA-256 and size and whether it comes from a group or the screen's own program, or `null` for an unpublished source; the `authorization` statement; and `nextSyncSeconds` (30). A suspended company renews nothing: the response has no statement and no desired publication, and the screen keeps its current state until its last statement expires. An unlinked screen receives `clearRequired` and nothing else, and continues with the devices module's erasure confirmation.
Manifest and media requests are allowed only for the screen's **current** desired publication. A superseded publication answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, and the player synchronizes again, which coalesces superseded work as the policies allow. Media responses carry the rendition's SHA-256 as a strong `ETag`, its exact length and type, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; the player verifies length and SHA-256 against the manifest before accepting a file. A screen may hold at most two media downloads at once.
Protocol compatibility: every manifest and exchange names its protocol. The sync request says which protocols the player supports; the server answers with the highest protocol both support and refuses with `PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED` when there is none. Only protocol 1 exists now. When a protocol 2 arrives, publications are serialized in both for at least 90 days (AT-26).

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: The authorization statement
text:
The authorization statement
Each sync response for an active screen carries a statement signed by the server as a compact JWS with `ES256` (ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256), a `kid` naming the key and `typ` `teluni-authorization+jws`. Its claims:
Claim
Meaning
`sub`, `company`
The screen and its company
`iat`
The server's time when it was issued: a signed time reference for the player's trusted clock (D-07, AT-16)
`exp`
`iat` plus seven days (AT-15), the latest moment the player may show protected content without a newer statement; capped by commercial validity in PJ-27
`publications`
The publications the player may activate or keep active until `exp`: each ID with its manifest SHA-256
`publications` holds the desired publication and, while the screen has not activated it, the active and recovery generations the screen reported, when they are unpruned publications of the screen's company. An unpublished source yields an empty list, so the screen shows neutral output after applying an assignment, as the policies require; a failed staging keeps the previous generation authorized. Revoking a specific publication (incident response) would remove it from every list; no revocation operation is part of this design.
The player obligations that follow, for PJ-12: verify every statement with a pinned key before trusting it; activate only a complete generation whose manifest SHA-256 a valid statement lists; show neutral output when the latest valid statement has expired by trusted time; never extend a statement's validity locally; keep the latest statement with the active generation.
Keys: `TELUNI_SYNC_SIGNING_KEYS` is a key ring of P-256 private keys, newest first. The first key signs; the public halves of all keys are served at `GET /device/keys` as a JSON Web Key Set. The player fetches the set after pairing over TLS and refreshes it at each sync when a statement names an unknown `kid`. Rotation adds a new key at the front and keeps the old one for at least seven days, the longest validity of a statement it signed. Without the key ring the publications module stays unmounted.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: State reports and monitoring
text:
State reports and monitoring
The sync request is the screen's report: the protocols it supports and its application version; the `active` publication with its activation time and the `recovery` publication; the `staging` attempt with its publication, state (`DOWNLOADING`, `VERIFYING`, `READY` or `FAILED`), bytes done and total and a failure code (`STORAGE_FULL`, `DOWNLOAD_FAILED`, `INTEGRITY_FAILED`, `INVALID_MANIFEST`, `INCOMPATIBLE`); the playback condition (`PLAYING`, `NEUTRAL`, `AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED`, `CLOCK_UNTRUSTED`, `DEGRADED` or `SETUP`); free and total storage; and the device's clock reading. All values are bounded and validated; unknown publication IDs are kept as reported but never trusted.
The server keeps the latest report per screen with the time it was received and the desired publication it answered, and appends an event when the active publication, the staging state or failure, or the playback condition changes, or when a newly desired publication is delivered. Events are kept for 30 days (AT-20).
The panel derives, never stores, what it shows:
**Connection:** online while the last sync is at most 90 seconds old, without recent contact after 90 seconds and offline after 120 seconds (AT-24), always with the time of the last contact.
**Publication:** up to date when the reported active publication is the desired one; updating while staging the desired one, with progress; failed with the reported reason; neutral when the source is unpublished; unknown when the screen has never reported.
**Playback:** the reported condition, labeled as reported by the screen.
The panel polls a screen's state every 5 seconds while its page is open, so an acknowledgement appears within AT-14's 10 seconds of the server receiving it.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: History, restore and retention
text:
History, restore and retention
A program's history lists its publications, newest first, with generation, publisher, time, counts and whether it restores an earlier generation. **Restore** publishes an earlier generation's content again as a new generation, after checking that its playlists still fit the program's current reach and its media are still publishable; it never changes the drafts. Restore needs the same capability as publishing.
A publication is **retained** while it is the latest of its program, while an active screen reported it as active, recovery or staging within the last seven days, or until 90 days after the next generation superseded it (AT-18). Hourly maintenance prunes the others: it deletes their manifest bytes and media references and keeps the row, so history still shows them as no longer restorable.
The publications module registers a `publication` media reference guard: media referenced by a retained publication cannot be deleted or purged, and the refusal discloses only references the caller may see. Deleting a group, which requires that it has no members, deletes its program and with it the program's publications; their audit events remain.

heading: Permissions
text:
Permissions

`publications.publish`: publish and restore programs

Scope follows the programming design: a group's program needs the capability on every branch of its span (company scope for a whole-company group), a screen's program on the screen's branch. `publications.publish` always needs strong authentication, also through a profile, and works in the normal session without a recent re-authentication. A program's history and check need `programming.view` on the same scope; a screen's synchronization state needs `devices.view` on its branch.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
At most 30 publications per program per hour and 300 per company per day (`RATE_LIMITED`; an unchanged publication counts for neither). Snapshots of at most 2,000 items and 1,000 distinct media. Sync requests share the device request limit, which counts each presented credential, not each client address, under a ceiling of 6,000 requests per address per minute, because screens behind one router or the ingress proxy share an address; at most two concurrent media downloads per screen. Reports are bounded by request validation.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Audit
text:
Audit
`publication.published` and `publication.restored` events record the actor's membership, the program, its source kind and branches, the generation and counts, in the same transaction. Pruning is maintenance and is not attributed to a person. Device reports are operational records with 30-day retention, not audit.

Every table carries `company_id` with composite tenant references, as the [tenant data design](tenant-data-design.md) requires; reported publication IDs are stored as reported, without references, because they are untrusted. Manifests are `CONFIDENTIAL` like the schedules they contain.

Contracts
Human operations under `/companies/{companyId}/programming/groups/{groupId}/publications` and `/companies/{companyId}/programming/devices/{deviceId}/publications`: list (cursor-paginated), `check`, publish with the content digest, and `{publicationId}/restore`. `GET /companies/{companyId}/devices/{deviceId}/sync-state` returns one screen's state and `GET /companies/{companyId}/publications/screen-states?deviceId=…` up to 100 for lists. heading: Panel
text:
Panel
**Programs** (group page and a screen's programming): the latest generation with its time and publisher, "changes not published" when the check reports a different digest, and **Publicar** for people who may publish: a dialog with the summary, the number of screens that follow the destination and every problem, then confirmation. A history list with **Restaurar** on retained generations.
**Screens** (Telas): a synchronization section with connection and last contact, desired and active generation, staging progress or failure, reported playback and free storage; the list shows connection and publication state per screen; a group page summarizes its members.

heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Domain tests: manifest serialization is stable byte for byte and matches the fixture rule format; content digest independence from generation and time; statement signing and verification with rotated keys; desired-state selection; authorization lists for desired, active, recovery, unpublished and foreign publications; connection thresholds; retention decisions.
Integration tests against PostgreSQL with two companies and differently scoped members: check and publish allowed and denied by role, profile and span; operators denied; digest conflict; unchanged publication; fades, deleted media, out-of-scope playlists and size limits refused; generations; media guard; restore; desired state across publication, assignment, individual programming and moves; the unpublished-destination confirmation; sync for active, suspended and unlinked screens; manifest and media access only for the current desired publication and the screen's company; ranges; reports, events and states; pruning after 90 days with retention exceptions; limits and audit rows.
Browser component tests for the publish dialog, history and restore and the screen's synchronization section, and one end-to-end journey in which a simulated player pairs, synchronizes, downloads and verifies the manifest, media and statement, and reports activation while the panel shows the screen up to date.

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-20 under [PH-25](human-actions.md#ph-25):
**Publication unit.** One immutable generation sequence per program; a publication copies the program's rules, its playlists and descriptors of its media; publishing needs the content digest the person reviewed, and unchanged content returns the latest publication.
**Derived desired state.** A screen desires the latest publication of its current source, computed at each synchronization; no fan-out; an unpublished source means neutral output; the assignment confirmation is required only for unpublished destinations.
**Pull synchronization (ADR-0030).** `POST /device/sync` every 30 seconds exchanges the screen's report for its desired state; manifests by publication and media by item, both only for the current desired publication; no push channel.
**Manifest protocol 1.** Exact JSON bytes identified by SHA-256, identifiers instead of names, rules in the fixture format, media descriptors with size, SHA-256, type and dimensions; zones delivered per screen.
**Signed authorization statement (ADR-0030).** ES256 JWS from the `TELUNI_SYNC_SIGNING_KEYS` key ring with signed server time, a seven-day expiry and the manifests the screen may play; public keys at `GET /device/keys`; the player obligations listed above.
**Publication validation.** Scope, media availability (archived allowed), schedule validity and size are checked again; fades are refused until a qualified profile exists rather than downgraded.
**Permissions.** `publications.publish` as in the table, delegable with `programming.view`, always with strong authentication and no recent re-authentication; history with `programming.view`, screen state with `devices.view`.
**Reports and monitoring.** Latest report per screen and 30-day transition events; connection thresholds of AT-24 from the last sync; reports are facts, never desired state.
**Retention and restore.** Retained while latest, reported in use within seven days, or within 90 days of being superseded; pruning keeps the history row; restore republishes a retained generation as a new one; a `publication` media guard protects retained media.
**Limits.** 30 publications per program per hour and 300 per company per day; 2,000 items and 1,000 media per snapshot; two concurrent media downloads per screen.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-11 in local and CI environments with a simulated player. It does not qualify any player behavior on hardware (PH-08, PJ-12), select alert channels (D-09) or provision signing keys in a real environment (PJ-13).

title: Teluni Publication and Synchronization Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**Fan out desired state into per-screen rows when publishing or assigning.** Makes reads trivial, but needs a durable queue to survive crashes between the publication and the fan-out and can disagree with assignments made in between; computing desired state from authoritative rows at each poll is always consistent and costs one indexed query per sync.
**Push (WebSocket or server-sent events) or a broker.** Faster detection, but AT-11 allows 30 seconds, and a persistent channel adds connection state, proxies and reconnection logic on a single-host pilot; polling also serves as the AT-24 heartbeat.
**Rebuilding the manifest on every request, or storing it as `jsonb`.** Either would change bytes between requests (PostgreSQL normalizes `jsonb` key order), so the SHA-256 the statement signs could not identify them; stored exact bytes are the immutable identity.
**Signing each manifest at publication instead of per-screen statements.** Authenticates content but not the screen's entitlement or time; a per-screen statement binds the screen, its allowed publications, the expiry and a signed server time in one verifiable object.
**Relying on TLS only.** TLS protects transport but leaves the stored expiry and manifest choice as plain files that a casual edit could extend; the signed statement makes them tamper-evident and gives the trusted clock a server reference.
**Ed25519 or HMAC statements.** Ed25519 is compact but not available on every Android version the player may target without an added library; an HMAC would put a shared secret on every screen. ECDSA P-256 is supported by Node.js and by Android's standard security providers.
**Publishing per screen instead of per program.** Would copy one group's snapshot for every member and lose the generation sequence a person reasons about; screens already share a program through their group.

Teluni Release Policies

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Decision status and ownership
text:
Decision status and ownership
**Decided on 2026-10-18:** these product policies consolidate the owner's questionnaire and the remaining choices explicitly delegated to engineering. They extend the earlier company-to-screen requirements to freeform composition and configurable catalogs. Product capability and quality take priority over reducing scope solely for an MVP label. None of these decisions proves implementation, hardware capacity or release readiness.
This document owns observable business behavior. [Acceptance targets](release-targets.md) own numeric limits and qualification goals; [playback/sync](playback-and-sync.md) owns the proposed delivery lifecycle; [architecture](architecture.md#pending-decisions) and ADRs own remaining technical choices. PH-08/PH-10/PH-11/PH-13 and PJ-07 retain their separate hardware, operations, identity, privacy and architecture reviews.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Assignment and publication
text:
Assignment and publication
Support individual-device assignment and persistent company-owned groups. A device belongs to zero or one programming group; a group may span authorized branches of the same company. Check all target references and permissions on the server.
A grouped device follows its group unless an authorized user explicitly selects individual programming. That choice replaces the complete group programming, retains membership and is visibly identified in the panel. Returning to the group is explicit; a membership edit does not silently remove the exception.
Confirming an assignment/source change requests the destination's latest published programming without another publish action. An intentionally unpublished destination is permitted after a clear pre-confirmation indication: after applying the authorized change, the player shows local neutral output until its first valid publication. A failed or unseen synchronization instead preserves valid state.
Ordinary layout, schema, record, playlist and schedule edits are drafts until deliberately published. An exception applies to an authorized **price save**: it automatically records publication intent for affected published bindings and produces a new validated version. A price save never mutates a snapshot in place or publishes unrelated drafts. This exception concerns designated monetary price semantics, not every numeric/custom field.
[PH-11 identity/access policies](identity-and-access.md#publication-impact-and-delayed-work) require whole-mutation rejection when any affected target is unauthorized, without partial distribution or automatic approval fallback. Optional company approval rules distinguish a proposal from the effective price save: only an authorized independent approval commits the effective price and initiates automatic publication. No proposal is reported as an already-applied price.
Distinguish saved, queued, failed, published, downloaded and active states. If automatic price publication fails, show the pending/failure state and retry/reconcile durably; do not report that disconnected TVs have changed. Duplicate saves/retries and concurrent edits must not replay an obsolete price over a newer one. Invalid input is rejected before accepting a price change.
A publication contains consistent layout/schema/record/price/media versions. Activation requires its complete supported resource set; failure preserves the last valid generation. Rollback still applies current authorization and content-validity rules and cannot resurrect an expired promotion.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Configurable catalogs
text:
Configurable catalogs
Catalogs are tenant-owned, user-configurable collections with typed field definitions and records. They are not restricted to product tables or a fixed mandatory set of product fields. Users can add fields and define required/optional values; products, menus and public weekly agendas are examples of reusable configurations. A weekly-agenda record describes displayed data and does not implicitly become a player publication schedule.
Provide reviewed field types for text, numbers, booleans, dates/times, selections, monetary values, authorized media and scoped record references as appropriate. Exact type schemas and storage remain technical design work. Validate field definitions, values, references, sizes and nesting. Customization does not permit arbitrary code, SQL, executable markup or unrestricted external data access, and does not imply unbounded resources.
Stable field identity and schema versions must preserve bindings. Renaming a label must not silently change meaning. A destructive schema/type change needs explicit migration/reference handling; published versions remain bound to their original validated schema and values. Importing/copying layouts or catalog definitions does not grant access to another company's media or records.
Product configurations can use description/image/category/availability, normal/promotional monetary values and variation/combo references without imposing those fields on an agenda or another catalog. This defines extensible data and presentation, not an ERP/POS transaction engine. Ordinary catalog edits retain draft/publication separation; designated price updates use the automatic publication exception above.
**Delegated commercial defaults:** a company-level base price may be overridden by branch. Every monetary value has explicit currency and exact representation; do not convert currencies automatically. Preview the effective branch value. A promotional price applies only within its published validity, then falls back to the normal price. Reject competing promotion periods for the same product/branch. Hide unavailable products by default; a component may explicitly show an unavailable indication instead. All of these rules must be evaluable from a valid offline publication.
Catalog views bind selected fields into a list/table/menu/agenda rather than relying only on flattened artwork. Support automatic pagination with configurable timing, grouping by an available chosen field and an explicit minimum readable text size, plus manual pagination. Never silently clip names/prices or shrink text indefinitely; an unresolvable overflow needs visible validation. Generic catalogs need no mandatory category or price field.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Composition and regional playback
text:
Composition and regional playback
Provide a freeform editor to create, position and resize simultaneous areas. A group is a programming source, not a limit on area count. Validate geometry, orientation, references and the supported rendering profile; do not silently drop a function to fit a device.
Layouts have a structured, versioned textual representation with validated copy/import/export, revision history and preview. Serialization, editor/renderer libraries and wire schemas remain subject to technical review; AI is not required.
Areas advance independently by default, with optional coordinated areas/pages. This owner-approved hybrid mode replaces compulsory whole-screen progression while retaining that capability when selected. Coordination within one TV does not approve synchronization across separate TVs.
Each area may have its own schedules and optional default. Its active schedule selects the area's content and is not overwritten by a global page transition. After the exception ends, return to the current page's applicable content, then its configured default, otherwise a neutral area; do not restart unrelated independent areas. Preview must expose these regional exceptions to page coordination. Coordinated page changes use one transition point for the participating page-controlled areas; a regional exception temporarily keeps its own eligible output.
When no schedule or default applies, keep that area's geometry and neutral background without automatically redistributing the layout. A complete programming source with no eligible output uses safe local no-programming output. Never borrow a group default while an individual override is selected.
Coordinated pages have explicit duration, with an automatic suggestion covering the longest video. Reject ordinary page durations that would cut a full video. Shorter videos finish and hold their last frame until the page changes; static content remains visible. Independent areas retain their per-item durations. Scheduled boundaries override ordinary completion and may interrupt any current item/page.
Support several concurrent videos subject to a measured device profile. Ordinary video playback uses its complete original duration; per-item trimming is not part of the selected baseline. Independent image items use the default/configurable bounds in the target specification.
Support individual audio mute/volume controls and multiple audible areas. **Delegated safe default:** newly created areas start muted and mixed audio requires deliberate configuration; do not impose a universal one-audio-area limit. Qualification must test the supported mix, output controls and recovery.
During an already-active presentation, isolate a rendering failure to its area: attempt bounded recovery, then show still-valid regional contingency content or neutral output, preserve unaffected areas and report the failure. Keep a coordinated group's logical page timeline; a failed area may rejoin at the current valid state instead of forcing every area to restart. Whole-generation staging/integrity failures remain distinct and preserve the previous valid generation.
Offer direct cuts and configurable fades with preview only on validated profiles. A fade never extends expired commercial content; when necessary at an expiry boundary use an immediate cut. Advanced effects remain separate scope.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Time and scheduling
text:
Time and scheduling
Use per-device local business time: explicit device timezone, otherwise the deliberately selected branch timezone. Never inherit the server host timezone. Cross-branch groups therefore interpret local recurring hours per target. Locale changes do not change timing.
Start instants are inclusive and end instants exclusive. Reject overlapping schedules competing for the same output/area; intentional concurrent content in different areas is permitted. Do not resolve conflicts by implicit priority, last edit or creation order. Backend preview and player must share fixtures.
Permit overnight windows anchored to the starting weekday: Friday 22:00–02:00 ends Saturday at 02:00. Date-only final validity includes that complete local day and ends at the next local midnight, clipping any overnight window at that limit. If Friday is the last valid day, its 22:00–02:00 window therefore ends at Saturday 00:00. Reject equal start/end times as ambiguous and provide a separate explicit all-day option.
Follow geographic timezone rules. For nonexistent local boundaries use the first valid instant; for ambiguous boundaries use the earlier occurrence for a start and the later occurrence for an end. Show the resolved result in preview, validate conflicts after resolving it and do not duplicate publication/execution solely because clocks repeat. Exact library/fixture implementation remains technical work.
When eligible scheduled output changes, interrupt the current item instead of waiting for completion. Apply this to the affected regional output or page-controlled coordinated participants; an unrelated independent area continues. Timing tolerances and trusted-clock bounds are defined in the acceptance targets, not claimed measurements.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Media and deletion lifecycle
text:
Media and deletion lifecycle
The acceptance targets define configurable ingestion bounds separately from supported playback profiles and commercial quotas. Validate declared and inspected file type, size, decoded dimensions, duration, compatibility and scoped references; exact allowed codecs/containers require D-05 review.
Preserve originals and create compatible renditions when validated processing is supported. Show preparation/progress/preview and keep publications unavailable until their required renditions are durable. If safe conversion is unavailable, reject with an actionable reason. Do not silently remove areas or distort content to compensate for an unsupported device. Processing isolation/tools/capacity remain technical and host-readiness work.
Archiving removes media from new selections but does not break existing references. Block physical deletion while referenced by drafts, active/staged/recovery generations or protected retained publications; disclose only references the caller may see. Assisted removal of draft references needs confirmation and never rewrites issued snapshots. Retention expiration alone is insufficient for garbage collection: reference protection, device reconciliation and the offline envelope must also permit removal.
Keep active and previous valid player generations plus valid staging resources. Preflight new resources and the reserved-space target; insufficient capacity preserves valid playback and reports required capacity rather than deleting protected resources. Deduplicate shared immutable assets when accounting for generations. Catalog schema/record/media references need the same reference-aware lifecycle; legal/privacy retention remains PH-13.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Offline authorization and clock trust
text:
Offline authorization and clock trust
[Commercial policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention) additionally bound future playback authorization by known trial/paid/grace deadlines; the shorter commercial or seven-day offline bound wins. This does not change already-issued unreachable leases retroactively, relax identity/security controls or select a credential mechanism. Commercial restriction, security suspension and confirmed erasure remain distinct.
The target specification fixes the maximum offline authorization interval and clock-uncertainty bound. After authorization expires, show neutral output and request reconnection. Revocation denies new protected server operations; an unreachable device may retain playback until its local authorization expires. Do not claim remote erasure while unreachable or extend authorization by restoring an older generation.
Detectable incompatible clock jumps or insufficient trusted time suspend time-dependent schedules/prices and produce neutral output with diagnostics. Do not guess promotional validity or claim all wrong clocks can be detected without a reference. Elapsed-time retries and business wall-clock time are separate. Reboot/offline trusted-time estimation and credential mechanisms require threat-model/technical review using established security components.
Unlink requires explicit authorized confirmation, server revocation and a distinct pending-clear state for offline devices. On reconnection clear private local content/configuration/credentials. Reassignment to another company requires verified cleanup or controlled reset before new pairing. Distinguish revoked access, unreachable device and confirmed erasure; failure/retry must never expose the previous tenant's data.

title: Teluni Release Policies
heading: Compatibility and updates
text:
Compatibility and updates
The target specification defines the protocol-generation support window. Reject unknown/incompatible interpretations clearly, preserve valid permitted playback and report actual versus desired versions. Updates require controlled distribution, a configurable window, qualified installation/recovery and verified rollback behavior. Never assume an untested app/data downgrade is safe. Urgent security exceptions must be explicitly reviewed and communicated; no store, installer or update library is selected here.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Governing controls and implementation boundary
text:
Governing controls and implementation boundary
**Decided requirements:** HTTPS, secure established authentication, server-side authorization and tenant isolation, separate device identities with revocable credentials, relevant audit, validated private media, recoverable backups, structured redacted telemetry and controlled updates. These are acceptance obligations; the foundation runtime alone does not implement tenant/device security.
Apply the inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md), [authorization](../security/authorization.md), [data classification](../security/data-classification.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md), [secrets](../security/secrets-management.md), [production access](../security/production-access.md), and [error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md) policies. Do not invent cryptography, token schemes or password implementations. Accepted [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) remains authoritative for human API access-token verification; Keycloak, server-managed sessions and scoped access are accepted under ADR-0024/ADR-0025 and the [identity/access policies](identity-and-access.md). PH-11 decision selection is complete; actual provider/session qualification remains PJ-24, and device-authentication design remains separate.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Actors and authorization
text:
Actors and authorization
The actor categories and capability allocation are **decided product policies** from the owner's 38 PH-11 answers. The [canonical identity policy](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix) owns the full matrix, custom profiles, scoped sharing, responsible-administrator approval, strong authentication, recovery/session limits and support rules. The first standard-role and tenant/branch access enforcement exists in the organizations module; [D-01 implementation status](tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status) and [D-02 implementation status](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) distinguish verified capabilities from the remaining policy scope. Device identities, code-based pairing, revocation and erasure tracking exist on the server side per the [device enrollment design](device-enrollment-design.md#implementation-status); the Android player and its device-side enforcement remain PJ-12. Custom profiles cover only the organization and device capabilities that exist today; administrator approval requests and support access remain pending.
Platform operation has no default unrestricted customer-content access. Customer support needs explicit scoped, expiring consent with its real actor; no impersonation is selected. Player identities remain separate, restricted to their own authorized assignment/media/reports. Public company signup and automatic activation are selected, with completed PH-12 policy selection and PH-13/PH-15–PH-19 readiness gates; no existing company can be claimed by matching an email domain or name.
Check membership, tenant ownership, branch scope, operation and current resource state on the server. Cover detail/list/search/count/export, uploads/downloads/previews, manifests, synchronization reports and caches. Scope background work and reference validation as carefully as direct requests. Never trust a caller's tenant/role field or rely solely on a hidden button.
The first product slice needs both allow/deny tests with two companies and differently scoped branches, including resource-ID substitution, mixed-tenant references, stale membership, privilege escalation, unsafe assignment and bulk operations. The organizations suite covers its implemented company/branch operations; assignment, bulk and catalog cases arrive with their owning modules. Custom catalog fields, schema definitions, record/media bindings and imported layouts are subject to the same enforcement. [D-01](tenant-data-design.md) records implemented composite constraints and the approved decision to defer row-level security with compensating controls and reevaluation before real customer data.
Designated price saves automatically publish affected published content under completed PH-09. Server authorization must cover both the data mutation and its distribution targets; a draft-only edit permission cannot silently acquire publication power. Expose that consequence in the editing flow, keep unrelated drafts unpublished and audit actor/scope/revision/outcome. The [selected impact/approval rules](identity-and-access.md#publication-impact-and-delayed-work) reject an entire out-of-scope price mutation without partial publication or automatic approval fallback. Optional independent approvals distinguish a proposal from a saved effective price. Automatic work cannot bypass branch or tenant checks; technical verification remains pending.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Pairing and device lifecycle
text:
Pairing and device lifecycle
Pairing codes must be temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device/enrollment intent, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; length/entropy/expiry are reviewed protocol decisions, not values invented in this plan. The claiming human must already be authorized for the destination company/branch. A displayed code is not an enduring device credential.
Use established platform protections for local credential storage, protected transport, rotation/revocation and controlled updates. Keep raw codes, tokens, signing material and credential-bearing links out of logs, public errors, screenshots and support bundles. Rooted/stolen or physically accessible devices are a separate exposure risk; offline playback cannot guarantee protection against a person who controls the hardware.
Revocation denies future server access; an unreachable device cannot receive an immediate wipe or new policy. [Selected release policies](release-policies.md#offline-authorization-and-clock-trust) and AT-15/AT-16 define the bounded authorization/clock behavior, distinct pending/confirmed erasure and verified cleanup/reset before another tenant's pairing. The device credential mechanism is selected in [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md); time estimation and hardware verification remain D-07. Do not claim instant remote erasure of cached data. No general remote shell or unattended support access is part of the release. [Commercial expiry/entitlement policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention) add the known trial/paid/grace bound without exceeding AT-15, retroactive unreachable revocation or a bypass for suspended identities. Explicit limited commercial access is not security suspension.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Initial data inventory
text:
Initial data inventory
This classifies anticipated data using inherited levels; exact field inventories and retention periods must be recorded with future schemas. Customer media is not automatically public just because it will appear on a physical display.
Anticipated data
Baseline handling/classification
Collection/retention purpose
Public marketing and deliberately public product documentation
`PUBLIC` after approval
Product communication; exclude secrets/customer examples
User contact/identity references, memberships, branch assignments
`CONFIDENTIAL`
Access administration; minimize identity attributes and review removal
Customer media, drafts, schedules, custom catalog schemas/records, prices, publications and file metadata
`CONFIDENTIAL` by default; restricted content requires explicit review
Private content, data-driven display and reliable distribution; reference-aware lifecycle
Device configuration, linked IDs, addresses and diagnostics
`CONFIDENTIAL` where linked to people/companies; minimize network identifiers
Fleet operation, security and troubleshooting
Credentials, refresh/session material, pairing secrets and signing/backup keys
`RESTRICTED`
Authentication/recovery only; dedicated protected storage and narrow access
Audit and operational telemetry

Attributable actions, incident investigation and reliability; bounded independent retention
The release does not require patient records, biometrics, card data, surveillance footage or other sensitive personal records. Configurable fields and a weekly-agenda view do not authorize collecting them; use public/synthetic events for examples and qualification. Prevent unsupported data collection and agree customer upload restrictions, purpose, retention/deletion/export, privacy notices, customer/operator responsibilities and incident handling under [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13). LGPD and international privacy applicability require qualified review against actual operation; this is not a legal compliance certification.
Catalog/layout imports and values are untrusted data. Validate type/size/reference/schema evolution and prevent arbitrary code, SQL, executable markup or implicit external fetches. Rendering text or selecting a typed reference must not expose private record/media access. Operational report/history defaults in the acceptance targets do not decide legal or security-audit retention.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Media and audit protections
text:
Media and audit protections
Validate type using trustworthy inspection as well as declared metadata; define size, dimensions, duration and supported codec/container bounds, safe names/paths and parser isolation. Arbitrary user uploads are not executable content. Malware/content inspection and processing tools are pending risk decisions; no unvalidated transcoding framework is selected. Download authorization must cover tenant/device/retained-publication access and prevent public object exposure.
Audit relevant membership/role changes, device pair/revoke/reassignment, publication and important media lifecycle operations with attributable actor, scope, target, time and outcome. Do not use sampled debug logs as the sole durable audit mechanism. Decide integrity, retention, authorized audit access and failure handling before implementing the affected actions. Expected failures have safe explicit errors; unexpected failures remain observable under the inherited error contract.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Internationalization
text:
Internationalization
**Decided:** engineering source/identifiers/docs remain English; interfaces must be designed for localization, initially `pt-BR` and `en-US`. Do not put user-interface copy inside domain rules or use translated labels as persisted identifiers. No i18n library is selected yet.
Separate message keys/parameters from display text, including validation, accessibility labels, device setup and operational states. Translate safely without permitting arbitrary executable markup.
Present dates, times and numeric values using the selected locale. User-facing server errors need stable codes and safe parameters rather than coupling business rules to localized sentences.
Explicitly model timezone per branch/device. PH-09 selected [calendar/DST behavior](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling), device override then deliberately selected branch timezone and per-target local business time. Never inherit host timezone. D-06/D-10 implement matching preview/player fixtures and qualify trusted-time behavior against AT-16; business policy is no longer an unanswered PH-09 choice.
Locale is independent of timezone, currency and country. Monetary catalog fields use explicit currency and exact representation with scoped branch overrides; precision/rounding contracts must be reviewed before schema implementation. Formatting is not conversion; no automatic exchange service is selected. A generic catalog is not required to contain money fields.
Localize units and numeric presentation without changing persisted semantic meaning. Currency, decimal/grouping separators, longer translations and different date conventions must be tested.
Define the Android schedule/time interpretation with the same contract fixtures as backend preview. Changing UI language must not change actual publication timing or tenant permission.
The identity web module establishes this boundary with a typed pt-BR/en-US message catalog, Portuguese by default unless the browser prefers English, without selecting a library (D-10 remains open). Localization of the existing foundation shell and documentation portal is not performed.

Branches, memberships, access profiles, grants and organization audit events; later devices, media, programming, catalogs and publications
Immutable `company_id uuid NOT NULL` and a tenant key `UNIQUE (company_id, id)`
Branch-scoped tenant-owned
Grant branch scopes; later devices and branch overrides
Tenant-owned plus `branch_id` referencing the branch through the tenant key
Platform operational
None in the first slice
Separate platform capability and accounts (P11); lifecycle metadata only, never implicit tenant-content reads

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Keys and relational constraints
text:
Keys and relational constraints
**Identifiers.** The backend generates an immutable random UUID for each row; it is the primary key and the public resource identifier, never authority. Clients cannot choose it.
**Tenant key.** Every tenant-owned table with its own `id` declares `UNIQUE (company_id, id)`. This is the only target that other tenant-owned rows may reference. Join tables and one-to-one extensions without an `id` (such as a grant's branch scope or a company's responsible administrator) cannot be referenced and need no tenant key, but their own references follow rule 3.
**Composite references.** Every reference from one tenant-owned row to another uses `FOREIGN KEY (company_id, <target>_id) REFERENCES <target> (company_id, id)`. A single-column foreign key into a tenant-owned table is prohibited. A mixed-company reference is therefore unrepresentable, independent of application predicates. An optional reference keeps the default `MATCH SIMPLE` semantics: a null target column means no reference, while `company_id` stays non-null.
**Immutable tenant.** The runtime role receives column-level `UPDATE` grants that exclude `company_id`, so no runtime statement can move a row between companies. Moving a device to another company is unlink plus new pairing (FR-02), never an ownership update.
**Tenant-scoped uniqueness.** Business keys such as branch names are unique within a company (for example `UNIQUE (company_id, lower(name))`, partial over non-archived rows where archival exists), never globally.
**Explicit referential actions.** Declare `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and `ON UPDATE RESTRICT` (Prisma `Restrict`) on every composite tenant reference. Prisma's implicit `SetNull` for optional relations would try to null the shared `company_id` and is never used on these relations. `CASCADE` is reserved for children inside one module whose lifecycle is genuinely owned by the parent, documented in that module's metadata.
**Cross-module references.** A downstream module may reference an upstream module's tenant key (for example future devices referencing `branches (company_id, id)`), following the module dependency direction. An upstream table never references a downstream one. Prisma requires a back-relation field on the referenced model; it is structural only, confers no read or write authority, and adapters never traverse it across a module boundary.
A structural test on the migrated database (catalog query, run with the integration suite) asserts rules 2, 3 and 4 for every table that has a `company_id` column. It fails when a new tenant table or foreign key omits the pattern, so the rule does not depend on review alone.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Request scope resolution
text:
Request scope resolution
Company-scoped operations carry the requested company in the path, for example `/companies/{companyId}/branches`. The path value is a request for a context, not proof of membership.
The session boundary ([D-02](identity-session-design.md)) supplies the verified principal and assurance.
The organizations capability resolves access with one current query joining the principal's active membership, the company's state and all unexpired grants in that company. It returns an opaque `CompanyAccess` value: company ID, membership ID, and each granted capability with its scope (whole company or an explicit branch set). Only the organizations capability can construct it.
No membership or a suspended membership returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for the company path, without revealing that the company exists. Members of a suspended company receive an explicit company-state denial (code defined in PJ-03), kept distinct from limited commercial access under the [commercial policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention). An in-scope actor missing a capability receives `PERMISSION_DENIED`. A resource outside the actor's scope is indistinguishable from an absent one (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
Access is resolved on every request from PostgreSQL without caching, so membership removal, suspension, grant reduction and expiry deny the next operation, within the 30-second bound selected in [P20](identity-and-access.md#ph-11-decision-record). Introducing a cache later requires a lifetime below that bound plus explicit invalidation, recorded here first.
Sensitive authority changes (membership status, administrator promotion or restoration, grant and profile edits, responsibility transfer) lock the company row first and then the involved membership rows in ID order (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), and recheck the actor's current membership and administrator grant inside that transaction. Concurrent authority changes in one company therefore serialize instead of racing, and the fixed lock order avoids deadlocks. Every authority-changing writer must follow the same order.
Downstream modules receive `CompanyAccess`, ask it whether a capability applies to a branch, and obtain a branch filter (all branches or an explicit set) to put into SQL. They never accept a company, branch or role from the request body as authority.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Persistence adapter rules
text:
Persistence adapter rules
Every adapter operation on tenant-owned data takes the company scope from `CompanyAccess` as a mandatory parameter and uses it in every `WHERE`, `INSERT` and conditional `UPDATE`. Single-row lookups use the tenant key (`companyId_id` in Prisma), never a bare `id` lookup.
Branch filters and other authorization predicates are part of the query before pagination, counting and ordering. Nothing is loaded broadly and filtered afterwards.
A bulk request resolves its complete identifier set with the scope predicate in one query. If any element is absent or out of scope, the whole request fails as not found, with no partial effect.
Caller-supplied references (for example the branches of a grant) are validated by the composite foreign keys as the final guarantee. A tenant foreign-key violation maps to the module's not-found or validation error and never discloses whether the identifier exists in another company.
Cursors are bound to company, principal and list scope, and current predicates still apply on every page.
Deferred work and durable intents record company ID and the attributable actor; the executor resolves access again before any effect (IA-13). Workers that act as the system have their own explicitly reviewed capability.
Derived keys (caches, search entries, media object locations, manifests) include the company ID. A storage location never authorizes access; media access is checked against the owning row.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Row-level security evaluation
text:
Row-level security evaluation
ADR-0018 requires evaluating PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) before relying on it or rejecting it. The evaluated mechanism was: enable RLS on each tenant-owned table with a policy such as `USING (company_id = current_setting('teluni.company_id', true)::uuid)`, keep the runtime role a non-owner (already true, because migrations own the tables), and set the tenant per transaction with `set_config('teluni.company_id', $1, true)`.
Concern
Finding
Mixed-tenant references
PostgreSQL performs foreign-key checks without applying RLS policies, so RLS alone does not prevent a row from referencing another company's identifier. Composite tenant keys are required either way
Connection pooling
The tenant setting is safe with the pooled Prisma/`pg` adapter only when transaction-local, so every tenant request must run inside an interactive transaction: extra `BEGIN`/`set_config`/`COMMIT` round trips and a pooled connection held for the whole callback
Principal-centric flows
Listing a principal's companies, accepting an invitation before a membership exists and public signup creating a company need extra policy keys or `SECURITY DEFINER` functions, enlarging the reviewed surface
Roles and migrations
The runtime role is not the owner, so policies apply without `FORCE`; the migration owner bypasses them for migrations/backfills. Integration tests already run as the runtime role, so policies would be exercised
Failure mode
A missing setting yields no rows, which fails closed
**Approved outcome: do not adopt RLS for the first slice.** The compensating controls are the composite tenant keys, immutable `company_id` grants, the mandatory scope parameter, per-request access resolution, the structural catalog test and the two-company adversarial suite below. **Reevaluate before PJ-14 admits real customer data or public signup**, when a second database consumer (worker, report or raw SQL path) appears, or immediately after any cross-tenant defect. Adapters already receive the scope, so adopting RLS later needs a new ADR, policy migrations and a transaction-local context in adapters, not contract changes.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Platform and administrative scope
text:
Platform and administrative scope
Platform administration is a separate capability held by individually provisioned platform accounts (P11), not a company membership and not a bypass of tenant predicates. The first slice exposes no platform routes. When added, platform operations may manage company lifecycle and commercial metadata; customer content requires an explicit, expiring, company-authorized support grant (P33/P34, IA-14) stored as tenant-owned data. Database, migration and backup access are operational access under [production access](../security/production-access.md), never product authorization.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Organization audit in the first slice
text:
Organization audit in the first slice
The organizations capability owns an append-only, tenant-owned audit table. Each membership, invitation, grant, profile, responsibility and company-setting change writes its event in the same transaction as the change, so a failed change leaves no event and a committed change exactly one. The runtime role receives only `INSERT` and `SELECT` on it, which makes rows immutable through the application. Events record actor principal and membership, action, target type and ID, outcome and allowlisted details, never secrets or full payloads. Branch events include the branch name at the time of the event, so later renames or name reuse do not relabel past changes; older events without that detail remain readable. Each event also records the branches it concerns (a branch change names its branch; a branch-scoped grant or invitation names its branches) in an append-only join table; an event without branches is a company-level operation. Company administrators read company scope; branch managers read only events that concern at least one branch and only branches they manage, so company-level events and operations that also reach other branches stay hidden. Retention, IP metadata and cross-module audit integrity remain [D-09](architecture.md#pending-decisions) and [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13); no deletion job is introduced.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Required verification
text:
Required verification
Every tenant-owned module reuses one synthetic two-company fixture: company A with branches A1 and A2, company B with branch B1, and principals for A's administrator, an A1 manager, an A1 operator, B's administrator, a principal holding memberships in both companies with different scopes, and an outsider. The first slice must show, against real migrated PostgreSQL:
Substituting another company's or branch's identifier in path, query or body returns not found, and lists, counts and cursors never include out-of-scope rows.
A direct runtime-role `INSERT` of a mixed-company reference fails with a foreign-key violation, and a runtime `UPDATE` of `company_id` is denied by privileges.
Membership removal or suspension and grant expiry deny the next request; no cached access survives.
A branch-restricted manager cannot act on another branch, and a bulk request containing one out-of-scope identifier is rejected entirely.
The multi-company principal sees only the requested company's data, and switching company relies only on the path plus current membership.
The structural catalog test passes for every tenant table and foreign key.
A failed authority change leaves no audit event; a committed one leaves exactly one, readable only within scope.
